questions.q: Does your name have any special meaning?
questions.answer: Yes, it does actually. My name carries a meaning connected to guidance and light, which is fairly common in our culture. I quite like it, because names here are usually chosen with real [[deliberation]] behind them.
My grandfather did, actually. In our family it's [[customary]] for the eldest relative to suggest a name, and my parents were happy to go along with it. I think that's quite a touching tradition.

Yes, like most people in Bangladesh, I have a short nickname that my family and close friends use. My formal name is really only for official documents, so the nickname feels far more [[affectionate]] and personal.

questions.q: What names are popular in your country?
questions.answer: Names with religious or poetic meanings are very popular here, particularly Arabic and Bengali ones. Recently, though, I've noticed parents choosing shorter, more modern names, which reflects a broader [[generational change]] in taste.

questions.q: Would you ever change your name?
questions.answer: No, I can't imagine doing that. My name connects me to my grandfather and to my family's traditions, so changing it would feel like losing part of my [[heritage]].
